text:
For a molecule to belong to the C₃h point group it must possess

1. a single C₃ axis,
2. a σₕ plane perpendicular to that axis,
3. but no C₂ axes perpendicular to the C₃ axis (otherwise the group would be D₃h).

A. Triisopropyl borate, B(O-iPr)₃  
–  The B and the three O atoms form a trigonal-planar (σₕ) framework with a C₃ axis perpendicular to it.  
–  Because each O atom is attached to an out-of-plane, asymmetric isopropyl group, the three possible in-plane two-fold axes are destroyed.  
→ Point group: C₃h.

B. Triphenyleno-trifuran hexaone  
C. Quinuclidine  
D. Benzo-trifuran hexaone  
All three of these molecules are either completely planar triangular frameworks or have equivalent threefold frameworks in which three perpendicular C₂ axes are present. Hence they belong to D₃h, not C₃h.

Only triisopropyl borate satisfies the requirements for C₃h symmetry.

Answer: A
